finding.title: Fix stale AC5 doc comment in epic_26_story_26_20 — still claims hebrewTerms/hebrewDate default to false

evidence.quote: /// AC5: hebrewTerms defaults to false, useHebrewDate defaults to false
'Story 26.20 AC5 — hebrewTerms and useHebrewDate default to true (issue-7a)',

finding.why: The file-level doc comment (written for the original story) still says defaults are false; the group title 184 lines below it, and the tests themselves — which correctly assert isTrue and match the live `defaultValue => true` getters in hebrew_terms_preference.dart / hebrew_date_preference.dart — were updated for fix(issue-7a) but the banner wasn't. A reader who only skims the file header gets the wrong answer.
finding.recommendation: Update lines 10-11 to state defaults are true, referencing fix(issue-7a).
acceptance_criteria: the file header's AC5 line matches the group title and the actual defaultValue getters

finding.title: Add a failure-path test for LearningOrderRepositoryImpl.saveOrder's transaction — only the happy path is covered

evidence.quote: 'saveOrder writes all items atomically — all rows present after call',

finding.why: AC3's group ('saveOrder is wrapped in a DB transaction') has exactly two tests: a happy-path write of 3 items (asserts all 3 rows exist afterward) and a source-grep for the literal substring '_database.transaction('. Neither exercises the actual point of a transaction — that a failure partway through rolls back the earlier writes instead of leaving a partial row set. A regression that replaces the transaction with a loop of independently-awaited inserts would only be caught if it also broke the happy path; the substring grep would even pass if the transaction call became dead/misapplied code.
finding.recommendation: Add a test that forces one write in the middle of saveOrder's upsert list to fail (e.g. a mocked ContentRepository throwing, or a constraint violation), then asserts zero rows were written — matching the rollback-verification pattern AC4 already uses ('saveOrder with isChildRestricted=true writes no DB rows').
acceptance_criteria: a test exists asserting that a mid-write failure inside saveOrder leaves the learning_order table unchanged (no partial commit)

finding.title: Make Epic-2 'table removed from schema' tests actually inspect the schema instead of schemaVersion

evidence.quote: test('content_items table is not in Drift schema', () async {

finding.why: Both tests are titled to assert a specific table is absent from the live Drift schema, but the body only checks schemaVersion >= 1 — true at every schema version that has ever existed, including hypothetical ones where the tables were never removed. If either table were accidentally reintroduced (e.g. a bad migration merge), neither test would notice.
finding.recommendation: Query the live schema (e.g. `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'` via db.customSelect, or Drift's `allTables`) and assert the two table names are absent.
acceptance_criteria: Test queries the live schema for the named table and fails if it is present
Reintroducing either table via a migration makes the corresponding test fail red

finding.title: Rewrite Epic-7 dashboard tests whose bodies don't exercise the behavior their titles claim

evidence.quote: test('points summary is excluded from state when userMode is adult', () {
// This tests the invalidation pattern — in the real app, ref.invalidate()

finding.why: 'points summary is excluded from state when userMode is adult' never touches the dashboard provider or screen that decides whether to render PointsSummaryWidget for a given mode — it only checks ProfileMode.adult != ProfileMode.child, true by enum definition regardless of any dashboard logic. 'pull-to-refresh triggers provider invalidation pattern' never calls ref.invalidate() or touches any Riverpod provider — it calls the pure CrossCurriculumAggregator.aggregate() function twice with different literal inputs, which trivially returns different output. If the dashboard's actual mode-gating logic or its pull-to-refresh/ref.invalidate() wiring regresses, neither test detects it, despite both titles claiming to cover exactly that.
finding.recommendation: Either move these under a widget/provider test that pumps the real dashboard screen or provider and drives the claimed interaction (mode gating via ConsumerWidget + ProviderScope, or ref.invalidate() via the actual pull-to-refresh callback), or rename the tests to describe what they actually verify (enum comparison, aggregator purity) so the suite stops overstating its coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Test titled around dashboard/provider behavior drives that behavior directly, or is renamed to match what it verifies

finding.title: Test breadcrumb trimming through the real _trimSederFromBreadcrumb, not a hand-copied mirror

evidence.quote:
/// Mirror of the private `_trimSederFromBreadcrumb` function in
    /// `active_track_card.dart`. Kept here as a pure-logic unit test...

finding.why: The 5-case 'Issue-8b' group tests a hand-typed copy of active_track_card.dart's private _trimSederFromBreadcrumb, not the function itself (it can't import a private symbol). The copy currently matches production, but nothing enforces that going forward — a future edit to the real function (separator change, RTL handling) can silently diverge from the tested copy while the suite stays green.
finding.recommendation: Extract the pure trim logic to a small `@visibleForTesting` top-level function (or a tiny core/utils file) that both active_track_card.dart and the test import — no widget pump needed since it is pure string logic, per Feathers' 'find the seam'.
acceptance_criteria: Test imports and calls the same symbol active_track_card.dart uses for breadcrumb trimming, with no duplicated algorithm in the test file
